column1: # The handoff key, pinned. Three tab-separated columns:
#   text      the input, with \n \t and \\ escapes
#   key       the expected speak_key() output: sha256( trim( text ) )
# This table is worth more than any prose about "the two sides agree": it is
# the only thing that fails if someone changes the trim, the hash, or the hex
# extraction in speak-key.sh. Both hooks source that one function, so both
# hooks inherit this table. §3.2 is the clause it holds down, and the failure
# it prevents is a plugin that is silently mute on every turn.
# The key column is generated by python hashlib -- a different language and a
# different sha256 -- so the test is a cross-implementation check rather than
# speak-key.sh agreeing with itself. Regenerate with:

column2: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
